card.text: Explore Deimos in 3D with cssEarth. Inspect mapped spacecraft imagery, elevation and the measured irregular shape of Mars’s moon.

introduction.text: Deimos is the smaller, outer moon of Mars. A blanket of fine debris gives much of its cratered surface a smooth appearance. It takes about thirty hours to orbit Mars.

normal.title: Multi-mission image mosaic
normal.summary: Photographed shadows, image seams and interpolated poles remain. Detail varies; missing coverage is not masked in this mosaic.

elevation.title: Shape-derived radial height
elevation.summary: Height relative to a 6.2 km sphere, from the 2023 shape model. Areas without a solved surface brightness are withheld.

albedo.title: SPC relative albedo model
albedo.summary: Relative brightness solved jointly with shape from mission images; this is the released SPC scale, not a natural-color photograph or a calibrated absolute albedo. Grid marks facets without solved albedo support; this is a conservative mask, not a complete image-coverage measurement.

slope.title: Modeled surface slopes
slope.summary: Slope relative to modeled gravity, using uniform density, rotation and Mars at the mean orbital distance. Values come from the released facet table. Grid marks facets without solved albedo support; this is a conservative mask, not a complete image-coverage measurement.
